title: Boss: read the load-test report
summary: A constant-rate load test of one API server lands in your inbox before a launch. Find the knee, size the pool, write the health checker, and diagnose what kind of limit the test hit.

steps.title: The report
body: The team ran `wrk2 -R` at rising rates against **one** API server (8 vCPU) in staging, 60 s per step, and
exported the results as CSV. The SLO is **p99 under 100 ms**; launch peak is forecast at **20,000 rps**.
Latencies are in ms and `cpu` is a fraction. The rows come sorted by `rps`, header first. Each step below is
checked by tests with this report and others like it.

steps.title: Find the knee
prompt: Write `int KneeRps(string[] rows, double p99LimitMs)`: skip the header line, then return the `rps` of the last
row **before the first row whose p99 is over the limit**. If no row breaks the limit, return the last row's
`rps`. If the first data row already breaks it, return `0`.
For the report above, `KneeRps(rows, 100)` is `4500`.
template: Dojo.Eq("never breaks a 5 s limit", 5500, KneeRps(dojoReport, 5000));
Dojo.Eq("breaks from the first row", 0, KneeRps(dojoReport, 10));

steps.title: Size the pool
prompt: Plan each server at a fraction of its knee, not at the knee. Write
`int ServersFor(int peakRps, int kneeRpsPerServer, double fractionOfKnee, int spare)`: the servers needed so
each one runs at `kneeRpsPerServer x fractionOfKnee`, **rounded up**, plus `spare`.
starter: int ServersFor(int peakRps, int kneeRpsPerServer, double fractionOfKnee, int spare)
solution: int ServersFor(int peakRps, int kneeRpsPerServer, double fractionOfKnee, int spare)
template: Dojo.Eq("tiny load needs one server", 1, ServersFor(100, 4_500, 0.7, 0));
Dojo.Eq("two spares for zone loss", 9, ServersFor(20_000, 4_500, 0.7, 2));

steps.title: The health checker
prompt: The new pool needs active health checks with thresholds, like HAProxy's `rise` and `fall`. Write a class
`HealthCheck`:
- `HealthCheck(int rise, int fall)`: a new server starts **unhealthy** (it must prove itself first).
- `bool Healthy` (get-only).
- `void Report(bool passed)`: count consecutive passes and consecutive failures (a pass resets the failure count
and the other way round). An unhealthy server becomes healthy after `rise` passes in a row; a healthy server
becomes unhealthy after `fall` failures in a row.
- `int Flaps` (get-only): how many times `Healthy` changed.
solution: public HealthCheck(int rise, int fall) { this.rise = rise; this.fall = fall; }
public bool Healthy { get; private set; }
public int Flaps { get; private set; }
if (!Healthy && passes >= rise) { Healthy = true; Flaps++; }
else if (Healthy && failures >= fall) { Healthy = false; Flaps++; }
template: bool[] dojoSeq(HealthCheck h, params bool[] reports) { var seen = new List<bool>(); foreach (var r in reports) { h.Report(r); seen.Add(h.Healthy); } return seen.ToArray(); }
Dojo.Eq("rise 2, fall 3", new[] { false, true, true, true, false, false, true }, dojoSeq(dojoH, true, true, false, false, false, true, true));
Dojo.Eq("single failures do not flap a healthy server", new[] { false, true, true, true, true, true, true }, dojoSeq(dojoBlip, true, true, false, true, false, true, false));
Dojo.Eq("rise 1, fall 1 follows every check", new[] { true, false, true }, dojoSeq(dojoOne, true, false, true));

steps.title: What kind of limit?
prompt: Before buying servers, find out **what** the test ran into. Write `string Diagnose(string[] rows)` (header first):
- the **knee row** is the first data row whose p99 is more than **3 times** the first data row's p99;
- no such row -> `"no knee: test at a higher rate"`;
- the knee row's `cpu` is `0.85` or more -> `"cpu: add cores or cut cpu per request"`;
- otherwise -> `"not cpu: check pools, locks and dependencies"`.
The report above has its knee at 5,000 rps (140 ms > 3 x 18 ms) with CPU at 0.89: CPU-bound. A knee at 40%
CPU means the server is waiting on something: a connection pool, a lock, a slow dependency.
solution: ? "cpu: add cores or cut cpu per request"
: "not cpu: check pools, locks and dependencies";
return "no knee: test at a higher rate";
template: Dojo.Eq("the report: CPU-bound", "cpu: add cores or cut cpu per request", Diagnose(dojoCpu));
Dojo.Eq("knee at 31% CPU", "not cpu: check pools, locks and dependencies", Diagnose(dojoPool));
Dojo.Eq("never bends", "no knee: test at a higher rate", Diagnose(dojoFlat));
Dojo.Eq("exactly 3x is not yet the knee", "no knee: test at a higher rate", Diagnose(new[] { "rps,p50,p95,p99,cpu", "100,5,8,20,0.1", "200,6,20,60,0.95" }));
Dojo.Eq("exactly 0.85 counts as CPU", "cpu: add cores or cut cpu per request", Diagnose(new[] { "rps,p50,p95,p99,cpu", "100,5,8,20,0.1", "200,6,20,61,0.85" }));
